Container.Name: JDWeb
Container.Overview:
JDWeb is an unofficial web interface for JDownloader, with live downloads, link grabber, captchas and settings in a fast browser app. It is not made by or affiliated with AppWork. Small image (< 40 MB), no connections except to your JDownloader.
Before the first start, change two advanced settings in JDownloader (Settings, Advanced Settings): "RemoteAPIConfig: Deprecated Api Enabled" = true and "RemoteAPIConfig: Deprecated Api Localhost Only" = false. Then restart JDownloader. JDownloader's network, IP and Docker settings stay as they are.
Then set JDWEB_JD_URL to http://<JDownloader-IP>:3128 and choose a network that can reach JDownloader.
First start: find the one-time setup token in the container log (Docker, then Logs), open the WebUI and create your account with it.
SECURITY: JDownloader's API has no login. Anything that can reach its address and port 3128 can control JDownloader, JDWeb or not. In a home network that means every device there. For stricter isolation use a Docker network that only JDownloader and JDWeb share, or share JDownloader's network with this container (Network Type "Container", so that the API stays on localhost). See the README on GitHub.
Note: the container starts as root (--user 0:0), gives the appdata folder to PUID:PGID (default 99:100 = nobody:users) and drops root at once. Keep the data folder on the cache or a pool (for example /mnt/cache/appdata/jdweb), not on the array path /mnt/user (FUSE).

Config.Name: Data (appdata)
Config.Description: Account, sessions and settings. Keep it on the cache or a pool, for example /mnt/cache/appdata/jdweb. Not on a network share or /mnt/user.

Config.Name: JDownloader address
Config.Description: Address of JDownloader's API: http://<JD-IP>:3128 (or http://<container-name>:3128 in a custom network both containers share). Choose a Network Type above that can reach this address. The API has no login: see the Overview.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User id that owns the appdata folder (Unraid: 99 = nobody).

Config.Name: Trusted proxies
Config.Description: Optional: address or CIDR of your reverse proxy (comma separated), so that X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto are believed. Needed for secure cookies behind HTTPS.
